steps.say: Say the disclosure and ask how you can help.
Ask for the account number and read it back in pairs.
Before anything else, check the area for an outage. If there is one, give its status and do not book.
Ask what the meter shows, in the caller's words.
If the caller smells gas, say the safety script word for word, then transfer.
Offer the first opening with the call-out fee in the same breath.
If the meter is new and the caller asks about the fee, a supervisor decides.
Book only on a yes to the read-back.
Say it is booked and that you are texting the details.
Ask if there is anything else, then close.

items.text: Customers affected by the storm will not be charged late fees for September.

Per Policy Memo 114, customers in the designated storm area who incurred late payment charges on statements issued between 1 and 30 September are eligible for a one-time waiver (max. $12) of late fees, subject to account verification.
items.spoken: Yes: if your bill was due during the storm, we can remove the twelve-dollar late fee once. Shall I check your account?

items.text: A technician visit carries a forty-dollar call-out fee.
items.spoken: A technician visit carries a forty-dollar call-out fee.

items.text: An estimated reading is used when the meter could not be read; the next actual reading corrects the bill.
items.spoken: When the meter can't be read, the bill uses an estimate, and the next reading corrects it.

items.text: Account 6042: electricity and gas bills due in September, both paid late; two late fees; storm area; no waiver in twelve months.
Account 7719: late fee removed under the storm waiver on 20 September; storm area.
